# DK Publishing API

Schedule social posts (Instagram, Facebook, Threads, YouTube, TikTok) from software. You describe
each post per platform; the service validates it, keeps it as a draft until a person approves it
(unless your key may approve), publishes it at the slot, and reports the result. A post is never
published twice.

## Use it in four calls

1. Learn the rules (do this first, and again if a post is refused)
   GET /v1/platforms            every platform, its formats, limits, options, connected accounts
   GET /v1/platforms/{name}     one platform

2. Upload each file once, then refer to it by id
   POST /v1/media?filename=reel.mp4        body = the file's bytes        -> {"media_id": "..."}
   POST /v1/media   {"url": "https://...", "filename": "reel.mp4"}   (public https link; we download it)

3. Check a post without creating anything
   POST /v1/posts/validate      same body as POST /v1/posts  -> {"valid": true} or {"valid": false, "problems": [...]}

4. Create it
   POST /v1/posts               -> 201 with the post and where each platform stands
   GET  /v1/posts/{post_key}    status (poll, or just check later)
   GET  /v1/posts               every post made through the API, newest first

Send JSON bodies with `Content-Type: application/json` (a missing or form label is tolerated on /v1/posts and /v1/webhooks).

Authentication: header `Authorization: Bearer dkp_...` on every /v1 call. The owner issues keys with
one of three rights: read < draft < approve. Draft keys create posts that wait for a person.

5. Know the rules before making anything, follow every post, hand over many at once
   GET  /v1/spec[?platform=&format=]   the whole contract: files, limits, options, accounts, timing, route,
                                       an example and a JSON Schema per format. spec_version = ETag (304 if unchanged)
   GET  /v1/overview                   every post (the Sheet's too): pipeline by state and platform, published,
                                       problems, next slots, plan_ends (the last planned slot)
   GET  /v1/calendar                   every post by slot; filters state, platform, source (sheet|api), from, to,
                                       limit (<=200). state=published = the history, newest first, with live_url
   POST /v1/posts/batch                {"posts": [...up to 20...], "dry_run": false}: each like POST /v1/posts,
                                       on its own; always drafts; safe to resend; media may be https links

## MCP (for AI agents)

https://<this host>/mcp/ with the same Authorization header. Tools: publishing_overview, list_posts, get_post,
publishing_spec (read key); submit_posts, cancel_post (draft key). No approve tool: a person approves.
Resources dkp://spec and dkp://guide; prompt publish_posts. Files are never sent through MCP: upload them
with POST /v1/media or use public https links.

## A post

POST /v1/posts
{
  "post_key": "eid-2026-reel-1",          your own unique id; sending it again is safe (see "Repeating")
  "label": "Eid reel",                    optional, internal
  "approve": false,                       false (default) = draft for a person to approve
  "variants": [                           one entry per platform (and account)
    {
      "platform": "instagram",
      "format": "reel",
      "caption": "Slow-cooked for Eid.",
      "media": ["<media_id>"],
      "slot": "2026-10-12T19:30:00+02:00",   when to publish: ISO 8601 WITH a UTC offset (or Z)
      "options": {"share_to_feed": true}     the format's extra fields, from GET /v1/platforms
    },
    {
      "platform": "youtube",
      "format": "video",
      "media": ["<media_id>"],
      "slot": "2026-10-12T17:30:00Z",
      "options": {"title": "Dum biryani in 40 seconds", "made_for_kids": "no"}
    }
  ]
}

Rules of thumb (the authoritative, current numbers are always in GET /v1/platforms):
- Each platform has its own formats, caption limit, media count and file types. YouTube has no
  caption: use options.title and options.description. TikTok needs options.privacy_level.
- One variant per platform+account. Omit "account" when only one is connected.
- The slot must be at least a minute ahead. Times without an offset are refused.
- Unknown fields are refused, so a typo is caught instead of silently ignored.

## Errors teach you what to change

Failures are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`. Validation failures list EVERY problem at once:

{
  "status": 422, "title": "The request has problems", "detail": "...nothing was created.",
  "problems": [
    {"path": "variants[0].caption", "code": "too_long", "limit": 2200, "actual": 2410,
     "message": "Caption is 2,410 characters; Instagram allows 2,200."},
    {"path": "variants[1].options.privacy_level", "code": "not_allowed",
     "allowed": ["public", "friends", "followers", "only_me"], "message": "..."}
  ],
  "examples": {"variants[0]": {"platform": "instagram", "format": "reel", "...": "a valid variant"}}
}

`path` points into your request. Fix the listed fields and send again. Codes: invalid, invalid_post_key,
required, too_many, too_long, not_allowed, unknown_platform, unknown_format, unknown_option, unknown_field,
unknown_account, account_required, unknown_media, media_expired (the file was removed a week after its post
finished: upload again), media_rejected (see `expected`), invalid_slot, slot_in_past, slot_too_far,
duplicate_variant, post_key_taken, unsupported_type, too_large, file_too_large (a file over the format's
max_bytes in GET /v1/spec), empty, filename_required, bad_url, fetch_failed,
storage_full, quota_exceeded.

Other statuses: 401 no/invalid key, 403 the key lacks the right, 404 unknown post, 409 conflict,
413 quota_exceeded (this key's upload space is full), 507 storage_full (server disk nearly full; uploads paused).

## Webhooks (optional: instead of polling)

POST   /v1/webhooks                          {"url": "https://you.example.com/hooks", "events": ["post.published"]}
                                             -> 201 with "secret" (shown ONCE; it signs every message). Leave events out for all.
GET    /v1/webhooks                          your webhooks (never the secret)
DELETE /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}            stop
GET    /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/deliveries the latest messages: status, attempts, http_status, error
POST   /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/ping       send a test message now

Needs a draft key. https and a public host only; a key may have 3 webhooks. We POST JSON:
{"id": "evt_...", "type": "post.published", "created_at": "...", "data": {"post_key", "variant_id", "platform",
"account", "format", "state", "status", "slot", "live_url", "handed_over", "reason"}}
Events: post.approved, post.published, post.failed, post.expired, post.needs_check (outcome uncertain: do NOT resend),
post.cancelled (also when the owner rejects it), post.invalid; and ping.
Headers: X-DK-Event, X-DK-Event-Id (same on every retry: ignore a repeat), X-DK-Delivery, and
X-DK-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>" with your secret>. Verify it and refuse a
timestamp older than 5 minutes. Answer any 2xx quickly; anything else is retried (1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h,
6 h, 24 h, then given up and the owner is told). HTTP 410 switches the webhook off. Delivery is at least once.

## Files on the server

512 MB per file; one key may keep 5 GB at once (413 quota_exceeded); uploads pause with 507 storage_full when the
server disk is nearly full. A file is deleted a week after its posts are finished: a post naming a deleted file
is refused with media_expired, so upload it again and use the new id.

## Repeating a request

post_key is the idempotency key. Send the same post_key with the same content again (after a
timeout, say) and you get the existing post back with 200 and `Idempotent-Replay: true`; nothing is
created twice. The same post_key with different content is 409 post_key_taken: to change a post,
cancel it and submit a new post_key.

## States

Each variant has a `state`: awaiting_approval, scheduled, publishing, checking, published, failed,
invalid, cancelled, expired. `live_url` appears once published. On some platforms (see `mode` in
GET /v1/platforms) a post is handed to a person on Telegram to publish by hand: `handed_over` is true.

## Approving and cancelling

A person approves your drafts, on the owner's review page (the videos play there) or in the Google Sheet's
Calendar tab. You cannot reach that page and must never ask for approval rights. The page groups a day's drafts by
post_key (one idea, up to one variant per platform) and shows the key name, caption, options, slot and every file,
so use one post_key per idea and give files and captions a person can judge at a glance.

POST   /v1/posts/{post_key}/approve   (needs the approve right) approve every draft of the post
DELETE /v1/posts/{post_key}           cancel everything that has not gone out; published
                                      or in-flight variants are left and reported as a conflict
